audit_findings.title: Capitalized interest breaks the equity-OE debt treatment
audit_findings.magnitude: $100.6 million of 2025 interest was capitalized, equal to 8.5% of the $1,179.3 million anchor; the uncaptured OE effect is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Capitalized interest bypasses earnings and therefore the equity-level OE interest charge. If it was also excluded as growth capex, OE omits the financing cost; after commissioning, the interest enters earnings and lowers forecast OE.
audit_findings.evidence: For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, total interest costs incurred were $ 170.6 million, $ 123.1 million, and $ 109.5 million, respectively, of which $ 100.6 million, $ 66.8 million, and $ 33.0 million, respectively, were capitalized .
audit_findings.explanation: The capitalization is demonstrated, but an OE error is not yet demonstrated because the record does not show whether the maintenance-capex adjustment captured the $100.6 million. The amount is large enough to affect estimated value, although its direction is downward and therefore would reinforce, rather than reverse, the valuation's conclusion that value is below the $242.06 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile cash interest, expensed interest, capitalized interest, and the maintenance-versus-growth capex adjustment for 2023-2025; then rerun OE with any omitted capitalized interest charged once and contractual interest expense modeled after capitalization ends.

audit_findings.title: The anchor is a transition-year result for the aluminum ramp
audit_findings.magnitude: $173.0 million 2025 aluminum operating loss, equal to 14.7% of the anchor; first-half 2026 aluminum operating loss was $114.45 million; steady-state effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Temporary commissioning losses depress anchor OE, while future ramp margins, working-capital investment, and sustaining capital are not represented by the model's generic 0%-5% growth assumptions.
audit_findings.evidence: During 2025, the results of this segment largely consisted of sales from the ancillary recycled aluminum deox-rod facility, as well as construction, start-up, and commissioning costs associated with the recycled aluminum flat roll products mill and satellite recycled aluminum slab centers.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated transition-year distortion and is reasonably capable of changing the valuation. The mill shipped only 15,000 metric tons in 2025 against 650,000 metric tons of stated capacity, while 2026 results show both rapid revenue growth and continuing losses. Removing temporary costs would raise value, but disappointing margins or greater working-capital and sustaining-capital needs could lower it.
audit_findings.action: Separate commissioning and startup costs from recurring costs; construct explicit aluminum scenarios using actual ramp shipments, realized margins, working-capital requirements, minority ownership, and sustaining capital; rerun all valuation scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter misses the December NPS step acquisition
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 pro forma parent net income was $1,189.831 million versus $1,185.595 million reported, a $4.236 million or 0.36% increase relative to the anchor; OE cash-flow adjustment is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The anchor includes only one month of consolidated NPS cash-flow adjustments, while earlier months contain the 45% equity-method interest; forecasts cover 100% ownership.
audit_findings.evidence: Operating results of NPS from and after December 1, 2025, have been included in the company’s consolidated financial statements within the steel operations segment.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, but the filed pro forma results indicate that its 2025 earnings-scale effect was only 0.36% of anchor OE. That is too small to change the valuation conclusion, even though maintenance capital and working-capital effects remain unallocated. The $6.5 million remeasurement gain must still be excluded consistently.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a 2025 full-year NPS OE bridge from the pro forma disclosures and 2026 cash-flow data, consistently removing pre-acquisition equity-method income and the $6.5 million remeasurement gain; reopen materiality only if incremental maintenance capital or working capital is substantially larger than the disclosed earnings effect.

audit_findings.title: Redeemable noncontrolling interests are an unbridged senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $143.259 million at June 30, 2026, equal to $0.99 per fully diluted share and 0.84% of the $17,137 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any redemption obligation not already represented in parent-attributable OE must be deducted in the common-equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Redeemable noncontrolling interests related to Mesabi Nugget (owned 86 % by SDI) are $ 111.2 million at December 31, 2025 and 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The missing bridge line is demonstrated, although whether a separate deduction is economically required depends on the OE ownership allocation. Even deducting the entire latest carrying amount would reduce base value from $118.52 to about $117.53 per share, immaterial beside the $123.54 gap between base value and the $242.06 market price. Settlement materially above carrying value is an unresolved possibility.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the USS and Mesabi redemption formulas and current settlement values, confirm whether parent-level OE excludes the related minority cash flows, and rerun the bridge only for any claim not already captured or materially exceeding $143.259 million.

audit_findings.title: Parent-common earnings may be mixed with consolidated cash-flow adjustments
audit_findings.magnitude: The 2025 difference between consolidated net income and parent-attributable net income was $1.716 million, or 0.15% of the anchor; the audit reports a greater-than-5% FY2016 gap; the D&A, maintenance-capex, and working-capital allocation effect is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Using parent-attributable earnings with 100% of consolidated D&A, maintenance capex, or working-capital changes creates an ownership-basis mismatch in OE and potentially in the historical trend used to support growth judgments.
audit_findings.evidence: Noncontrolling and redeemable noncontrolling interests represent the noncontrolling owners' proportionate share in the equity, income, or losses of the company’s majority-owned or controlled consolidated subsidiaries.
audit_findings.explanation: The differing accounting bases and the FY2016 gap are demonstrated, but the record does not allocate cash-flow adjustments among the 75%, 86%, 94.4%, and 95% controlled subsidiaries. Consolidated add-backs can overstate value, while deducting consolidated capital requirements can understate it. The small 2025 earnings gap alone does not establish the net OE effect.
audit_findings.action: Reperform every OE year on a parent-common basis, allocating D&A, maintenance capex, and working-capital changes by subsidiary and ownership percentage; then recompute the trend, 2025 anchor, and all scenarios without changing the valuation methodology.
